images.name: looking-like-a-moron
images.alt: Cartoon Gravel God grins beside the words "Because I was scared of looking like a moron."
images.joke: Because I was scared of looking like a moron.

images.name: damn-kids
images.alt: A cyclocross racer climbs a snowy course past a crowd; cartoon Gravel God rides alongside shouting "Damn kids!."

images.name: still-open
images.alt: Cartoon Gravel God, seen from behind at night, asks a lit-up convenience store "You guys still open?"

images.name: try-new-things-1
images.alt: Cartoon Gravel God rides a sandy desert trail behind a mountain biker, groaning "Uggggh I don't have to steer on Zwift."
images.joke: Uggggh I don't have to steer on Zwift.

images.name: still-havent-done-cyclocross
images.alt: Cartoon Gravel God, thoughtful, with speech bubbles: "Why? I never did cyclocross, EVEN TO THIS DAY!", a small figure asks "Y tho?", and he answers "I didn't want to look like a clown."
images.joke: Why? I never did cyclocross, EVEN TO THIS DAY! / Y tho? / I didn't want to look like a clown.

images.name: foreclosed-identity
images.alt: Cartoon Gravel God, arms crossed, stands on a farm road beside text: "Because allowing your identity to foreclose around a rigid cycling identity prevents the acquisition of skills, abilities, and experiences that will make you better at bikes in general, which indirectly benefits performance in your preferred cycling discipline."

images.name: profile-look
images.alt: Cartoon Gravel God in profile, head and shoulders, looking off to the right.

images.name: good-beats-world-class
images.alt: Cartoon Gravel God grins beside text: "Because in most things, good is just as good as world-class, not because being good within a discipline is close to world-class, but because being good in many disciplines makes you world-class compared to most people."

images.name: practice-what-you-preach
images.why: Photo of his daughter with a speech bubble; no cartoon.

images.name: try-new-things
images.alt: Cartoon Gravel God, seen from behind, at a fork in a snowy trail: one sign says "TRY NEW THINGS", the other "DON'T GROW".
